title: Tenant-aware log forwarding & schema normalization pipeline
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem:
Current log ingestion accepts heterogeneous vendor log formats and freeform text blobs which causes: noisy dashboards, poor correlation with traces, inability to enforce per-tenant access controls, and high storage costs due to unstructured payloads.

Goal:
Implement a tenant-aware forwarding and normalization stage in the log pipeline that:
- extracts tenant_id / org_id from HTTP metadata or auth headers,
- normalizes incoming logs to a small canonical JSON schema (rwi_log.v1),
- attaches trace_id/span_id when available, and preserves original_raw for debug only,
- routes lightweight metrics to Loki for fast querying and full logs to ELK for searchable archives,
- provides backpressure and validation to avoid pipeline poisoning from malformed events.

Success criteria / acceptance_criteria:
- >=95% of production log volume conforms to rwi_log.v1 within 2 weeks of rollout;
- all log entries include tenant_id and at least one of (trace_id, request_id) when provided by client;
- no increase in 99th percentile ingestion latency by >20ms after enabling normalization;
- per-tenant retention policy enforced in downstream storage and visible in Console;
- canary rollout shows no increase in error rates or cost beyond expected thresholds.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- We normalize to a compact schema (rwi_log.v1) to keep index cardinality low; original_raw is optional and stored in ELK only when size < 64KB to prevent abuse.
- Tenant extraction priority: auth header > X-Org-Id header > body.metadata.org. If not present, mark as "unknown" and route to quarantined bucket for manual review.
- Use OpenTelemetry Collector as the normalization entrypoint with a custom processor that performs tenant extraction, schema mapping, and basic PII redaction; this leverages existing vendor integrations.
- For routing: metrics and small structured fields go to Loki (labels + minimal log line) for fast dashboards; full JSON documents go to ELK/Opensearch for search and long-term retention.
- Backpressure: the processor implements token-bucket-based throttling and a dead-letter queue (S3) for malformed or oversized events.

Implementation notes:
- New repo: infra/log-ingest-processor (prototype in branch: feat/tenant-normalize).
- Processor components: tenant-resolver, schema-transformer, trace-enricher, validation+throttle, router.
- Use vector for lightweight hosts and OTEL-collector for centralized gateways. The custom processor runs as an OTEL extension for centralized enforcement.
- Feature flag: observability.tenant_normalization (rollout groups: internal -> staging -> 10% prod -> 100% prod).
- Configurable retention and routing rules stored in Redwood Config Service (RCS) so product can change per-customer retention without deploy.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit tests for schema transform and tenant extraction (edge cases: nested JSONs, arrays, binary payloads).
- E2E in staging with synthetic multi-tenant traffic covering all vendor formats (CloudWatch, Datadog forwarder, Syslog, JSON over HTTP).
- Load test against a 2x projected QPS to validate throttling and latency.
- Canary rollout with real traffic to 5% of hosts, monitor: ingestion error rate, per-tenant missing-id rate, Loki query latency, and ELK indexing errors.
- Gradual expansion if canary metrics stable for 48h; rollback immediately if customer-facing errors spike.

Operational considerations:
- Observability: dashboards for (a) normalized-valid % by tenant, (b) missing-id rate, (c) processor latency distribution, (d) dead-letter queue growth, (e) per-tenant storage estimates.
- Alerts: missing-id rate > 2% for 30m, dead-letter queue growth > 1000/hr, processor CPU > 75% sustained.
- Audit: log transformations must be reversible for debugging (original_raw reference id to ELK). Access controlled via RBAC.

Open questions / risks:
- PII redaction rules: do we maintain a company-managed list or allow tenants to supply their own? (security wants company-managed minimum).
- Cost trade-offs: how many tenants require retaining original_raw? Default to off, allow opt-in paid feature.
- Compatibility: some vendor forwarders (legacy Syslog) will send huge freeform lines; we must reliably truncate and route to DLQ to avoid crashes.

References & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Log+Normalization+Design (design spec + schema rwi_log.v1)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412 (initial processor prototype)
- Grafana dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs-log-normalization/staging-overview
- Incident notes (related): https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-01-log-spam (lessons learned)
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Kapoor: Triage complete. Initial design doc linked in description. Priority set to P1 due to customer-facing cost and reliability impacts.
2026-02-18 - Ben Friedman: Design review done with infra and security. Agreed to use OTEL collector extension and DLQ on S3. Security requested company-managed PII redaction as minimum.
2026-02-24 - Infra: Prototype created (infra/log-ingest-processor). Basic tenant_resolver + schema transformer passes unit tests. Benchmarks show +6ms median overhead.
2026-03-02 - QA: Staging E2E run completed. Found edge-case with nested vendor metadata where tenant_id was missed; fix merged in PR #419.
2026-03-05 - Ben Friedman: Opened canary rollout (feature flag -> 5% hosts). Monitoring alerts configured in Grafana and PagerDuty.

2026-03-10 - Observability: Canary at 5% for 72h. Normalization rate 93% (below target); root cause: two legacy forwarders sending text-only Syslog. Added extra parser fallback and increased default DLQ capacity.

2026-03-12 - Ben Friedman: After fallback parser improvements, normalized rate increased to 97%. Proceeding to 25% rollout pending infra greenlight. Added follow-up ticket to product for retention billing option (PM-5247).
